knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the customer buys the finished look and the certainty that it will be done at their place. Hourly rates, kit and the business's age are not what is bought.
The lesson says a guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford, and that a fix-first window must be one you can keep. An open-ended or impossible guarantee does not meet this.
The lesson says a result claim, such as less breakage after colour, should not be published until you have evidence you can show. A famous endorsement, a discount or no evidence does not support it.

practicalCriteria: Applies the step to a real or simulated business decision and records the outcome
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate

stopWorkCriteria: Not applicable: business guidance; stop if an offer would make an unsubstantiated or misleading claim
